sentences.text: Natwar Bardhan vs State Of Bihar on 10 January, 2017

Author: Rongon Mukhopadhyay
Bench: Rongon Mukhopadhyay
 Criminal Revision No. 272 of 1999 (R)

In the matter of an application under Section 397 and 401
 of the Code of Criminal Procedure
 ---

Natwar Bardhan son of Late Krishna Chandra Bardhan
 resident of village Pupunki, Ps Chas (M), District Bokaro
 ... ... Petitioner

Versus
 The State of Bihar ... ...
Opposite Party

---
 For the Petitioner : Mr. A. K. Sahani, Advocate
For the Opposite Party : Mr. Arun Kumar Pandey, A.P.P.

PRESENT:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RONGON MUKHOPADHYAY

---
5/10.01.2017 Heard Mr. A. K. Sahani, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. Arun Kumar Pandey, learned A.P.P. for the State.

In this application, the petitioner has challenged the judgment dated 03.07.1999 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge II, Bokaro at Chas in Cr. Appeal No. 103 of 1996 affirming the judgment dated 09.08.1996 passed by the learned S.D.J.M., Bokaro at Chas in P.F.Case No. 24 of 1990 whereby the petitioner has been convicted for the offence punishable under Sections 16(i) (a) (ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and sentencing him to undergo S. I. for three months.
It has been submitted that the petitioner had a licence for running the shop and the same had expired at the time when the inspection was made.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge II, Bokaro at Chas
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It has also been submitted that no charge has been framed under Sections 16(i) (a) (ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
He further submits that out of the sentence of 3 months, the petitioner has remained in custody for 4 days.
Learned A.P.P. for the State opposed the prayer made by the learned counsel for the petitioner.

It appears from the allegation that the tea shop of the petitioner was inspected and at the time when the inspection was made, it was found that the licence which was produced by the petitioner has lapsed more than 3 years back.

Three prosecution witnesses have been examined in course of trial who supported the prosecution case and since the petitioner was found to be running a shop without a valid licence, the petitioner was convicted for the offence punishable under Sections 16(i) (a) (ii) of Natwar Bardhan vs State Of Bihar on 10 January, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17507236/
1 the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and was sentenced to undergo S.I. for 6 months.

entities.text: Natwar Bardhan vs State Of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the judgment passed by the learned trial court, the petitioner has preferred criminal appeal in Criminal Appeal No. 103 of 1996 in which while affirming the order passed by the learned trial court sentence was modified and reduced to S.I. for 3 months along with a fine of Rs. 1,000/-.

Since the allegation made in the complaint was substantiated in course of trial as the petitioner was running the tea stall without there being a valid licence, no interference is necessitated in the impugned judgment.

However, since the petitioner has remained in custody for a period of 4 days and he has faced rigors of trial since 1989, it would be in the fitness of thing that without interfering in the judgment of conviction, order of sentence is modified to the period which has already been undergone by the petitioner in custody.
This application is therefore, disposed of with the aforesaid modification in the sentence.

(Rongon Mukhopadhyay, J) R.Shekhar/NAFR/Cp. 3 Natwar Bardhan vs State Of Bihar on 10 January, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17507236/
